name: Addis Ababa
subtitle: Addis Ababa, capital of Ethiopia: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: About 3,859,999 people live in Addis Ababa (counted 2022).
Addis Ababa, meaning 'New Flower' in Amharic, was founded in 1886.
Empress Taytu Betul, wife of Menelik II, is credited with selecting the site and with naming (renaming) the place.

parts.text: Addis Ababa, meaning 'New Flower' in Amharic, was founded in 1886.
Empress Taytu Betul, wife of Menelik II, is credited with selecting the site and with naming (renaming) the place.
The OAU was created at a meeting in Addis Ababa in May 1963; its successor, the African Union, was launched in Durban in 2002.
The OAU's founding date was 25 May 1963 and it was formed in Addis Ababa.

blocks.prompt: About how many people do you think live in Addis Ababa?

parts.text: 3,859,999 in 2022, according to the figures compiled from the national statistics office. Which area is counted matters: Projected population of the Chartered City of Adis Abeba as of 1 July 2022 (Ethiopian Statistics Service projection; 2007 census count was 2,739,551).

items.text: The new Holy Trinity Cathedral is completed after Haile Selassie's return from exile.
Leaders of 32 independent African states meet in Addis Ababa to create the Organization of African Unity.
Lucy is found by U.S. paleoanthropologists Donald Johanson and Tom Gray (now kept at the National Museum in Addis Ababa).
The Red Terror Martyrs' Memorial Museum is established at Meskel Square.
The Adwa Victory Memorial is inaugurated in Addis Ababa.
